document.tekst_begin: Tweede Kamer der Staten-Generaal 2 Vergaderjaar 2025–2026 Aanhangsel van de Handelingen Vragen gesteld door de leden der Kamer, met de daarop door de regering gegeven antwoorden 2939 Vragen van het lid Van der Werf (D66), Van Lanschot (CDA) en Piri (PRO) aan de Minister van Buitenlandse Zaken over de uitspraken van de Israëlische Minister Ben-Gvir dat dagelijks tientallen Palestijnen gedood zouden moeten worden (ingezonden 19 augustus 2026). Antwoord van Minister Berendsen (Buitenlandse Zaken) (ontvangen 4 september 2026). items.titel: Construction of Dynamic Ecological Networks in Large-Scale Open-Pit Mining Areas on the Loess Plateau
items.samenvatting_bron: The Loess Plateau is a typical ecologically fragile area, where long-term intensive open-pit mining triggers severe vegetation loss, habitat fragmentation, and biodiversity decline. Although ecological network analysis integrating circuit theory and complex-network topology has become a mainstream connectivity assessment tool, existing studies mainly focus on urban agglomerations, nature reserves, and mountainous regions. Long-term dynamic networks considering mining and reclamation remain insufficiently understood in large coalfields. Taking the Pingshuo mining area as a case, this study combined MSPA, the MCR model, circuit theory, and complex-network approaches using remote-sensing images (1985, 1995, 2005, 2015, 2025), DEM, and road data to analyze 41-year spatiotemporal changes and propose a 2025 optimization plan. Ecological source proportion dropped from 6.17% (1985) to 3.56% (2015), then recovered to 9.79% (2025), dominated by forests and grasslands. Corridor length declined from 150.90 km to 99.32 km, and the 2025 network showed an average degree of 1.82 and an average path length of 1.45, indicating fragility. Under the proposed optimization scenario, node connectivity and network stability were projected to improve substantially. This study reveals how mining and restoration jointly shape ecological networks, offering a model-based theoretical framework for ecological security planning in similar fragile mining regions.

items.titel: Diminishing cooling returns of urban greening amid a warming climate
items.samenvatting_bron: Urban greening is widely prioritized as a nature-based solution to mitigating intensifying heat extremes in the context of climate change, yet its long-term global efficacy remains inadequately quantified. Here we present a two-decade assessment of vegetation dynamics and associated cooling effects across 3,806 urban clusters worldwide, integrating multisource satellite observations with ground measurements from 4,855 meteorological stations. We identify a pronounced climate equity gap: While cities in the Global North have largely expanded green infrastructure, they exhibit cooling saturation with diminishing biophysical returns. Conversely, most cities in the Global South show vegetation stagnation or loss, compounding rapid warming trends. This asymmetry exposes a critical climate justice challenge, indicating that current greening efforts are insufficient to offset a warming trend. Our findings underscore the necessity for context-specific, integrated climate adaptation frameworks that address both the quantity and quality of urban vegetation to achieve equitable thermal resilience in an increasingly warm world.

items.titel: ECOLOGICAL CHALLENGES AND CLIMATE CHANGE IN TÜRKİYE: RISKS, SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT AND ADAPTATION STRATEGIES
items.samenvatting_bron: This article examines the principal environmental challenges facing Türkiye in the context of climate change and considers policy options for strengthening ecological security and sustainable development. Based on a qualitative review of international assessments and national climate policy documents, the study analyses water stress, drought, extreme heat, wildfires, floods, coastal risks, biodiversity loss and greenhouse-gas emissions. It discusses the relationship between climate vulnerability and economic sectors, particularly energy, agriculture, urban infrastructure and tourism. The analysis highlights the importance of combining mitigation measures with adaptation planning, including renewable energy, energy efficiency, integrated water management, climate-resilient agriculture, early-warning systems and nature-based solutions. The article concludes that an integrated, evidence-based approach can reduce climate risks while supporting economic resilience and a fair green transition.
